_comment: Binding court directives that no test names BESIDE the order, from
This file waives COURT ORDERS, so it is held to a higher bar than the other exemption
files, not a lower one: every entry names an owner, an expiry, and a reason that says
WHICH KIND of unbound this is and what binding it would take. 'It is fine' is not a
Baselined 2026-07-26. RE-BASELINED the same day, upward, after the gate found a flaw in
itself: it had been matching an order and a directive anywhere in the same FILE, and its
own new test file - which names six orders - cross-matched immediately. Whole-file
matching counted 57 directives bound; requiring the directive to sit within two lines of

its order counts 36 - and exposed that six section labels named the order loosely ('COUNTY 10 D1') rather than by a key the gate resolves, which relabelling fixed, taking the bound count to 55. The larger number was wrong and this file was too short. A gate that
measures debt is the last place an over-count is tolerable.
So: 102 binding directives, 55 bound, 47 recorded here. The number may only go down.
Three of the classes below are bindable work that has not been done. One is not: a
Principal gate on a live cutover cannot be decided by CI, and a test claiming otherwise
would be precisely the false claim this gate exists to catch.

SUPPLY-CHAIN-ADVISORY-ACCEPTANCE-001:D4.reason: Not testable yet and correctly so: the duty engages only WHEN rclone ships a release carrying golang.org/x/text >= 0.39.0 (repin deploy/backup.Dockerfile's digest and drop both acceptances in the same change). No released upstream artefact carries the fix today, so no repo test can run the repin; what stops silence before expiry is already mechanical - an expired entry fails `make python-audit` (IAC-006) and trivy's expired_at returns the finding to the release gate. Binding arrives with the repin change itself.

HITL-NOTIFICATION-ROUTING-001:D4.reason: Not code-testable and correctly so: D4 binds the LIVE Classical Visas tenant - provisioning its delivery data (notification_prefs, bindings, channel) and evidencing a delivery artefact addressed to info@classicalvisas.com by a SELECT on the tenant database. Nothing in this repository can decide what a remote tenant database holds, and a test that claimed to would be the false claim this gate exists to stop. Discharged by the tenant record, not by CI.

OPERATOR-SEAT-001:D8.reason: Not code-testable and correctly so, and this one is unbound because it is UNPERFORMED rather than merely unbindable. D8 orders that a control.invitation.create for a second operator-side human be raised and actually put to info@classicalvisas.com on a >=24h window, and it states its own checkable: a SELECT on the Classical Visas database finding either a hitl_responses row from the client, or a hitl_requests row for that verb with (timeout_at - created_at) >= 24h and status='timed_out'. Nothing in this repository can decide what a remote tenant database holds. It is also the directive on which the RESERVED seat-operator question turns - that question becomes arguable only on a record showing D8 satisfied and the client having declined or failed to respond - so a test asserting it discharged would manufacture the very record the court said must be earned. Raising it is an outward-facing act on a live client tenant naming a third party, and is the Principal's to authorise. Discharged by the tenant record, not by CI.

AUDIT-DEPTH-001:D8.reason: Not code-testable and correctly so: it is a PRINCIPAL GATE on a live cutover or an external credential. Nothing in this repository can decide whether the Principal has given the go, and a test that claimed to would be the false claim this gate exists to stop. Enforced by the deploy record, not by CI.

CODEX-APPROVAL-ROUTING-001:A1.reason: An appellate directive with no engineering consequence by its own terms - the appeal affirms the deployed order, varies the record, or is expressly obiter ('commended not ordered'). There is nothing for a test to bind to; binding one would misrepresent obiter as ratio.

DEVELOPMENT-POSTURE-001:D7.reason: Not code-testable, and BLOCKED on the Principal - both facts matter. D7 orders that the Classical Visas client be told a control approval was cleared with no independent reviewer, and that the invocable surface over her data went from 99 verbs to 443. Discharge is a delivery artefact on the LIVE tenant database (a channel_outbox row addressed to info@classicalvisas.com), exactly as HITL-NOTIFICATION-ROUTING-001:D4 above: nothing in this repository can decide what a remote tenant database holds, and a test claiming to would be the false claim this gate exists to stop. WHAT BINDING IT WOULD TAKE: the same SELECT-based evidence that order's D4 takes, run against the CV database, recorded in this order's implementation_note. WHY IT HAS NOT BEEN DONE: the Principal has a standing instruction not to email this client. Nothing has been sent and nothing will be until he directs the channel or relays it himself - an agent does not resolve a conflict between a court order and a Principal instruction by picking the one it prefers. Per that order's forbidden list, a hitl_requests row that expires unheard satisfies nothing.

DEVELOPMENT-POSTURE-001:D8.reason: PARTLY discharged and partly not code-testable, so it is waived rather than claimed. D8 has three limbs. (a) Withdraw F7 from SUBMISSION-2026-07-29-083653: an amendment to a filed record, which no test can assert. (b) Account for docs/proposals/DEV-POSTURE-001-draft.yaml, cited in 881a9df's Refs trailer and existing nowhere - DONE, by recording its absence in scripts/check_prose_references.py's ALLOW with the reason, so the gate now carries the finding rather than the finding being lost. A commit message is immutable, so the historical half can never be more than recorded. (c) The forward-looking gate asserting every path in a Refs: trailer resolves in-tree - THIS IS GENUINELY TESTABLE AND IS NOT YET WRITTEN. WHAT BINDING IT WOULD TAKE: that gate, plus its seeded-failure suite, plus a decision on the historical offenders it finds (a gate red on arrival needs a ratchet, not a green claim). It is the standing cure for a defect class now at its third instance (INV-8, C1-C9, DEV-POSTURE-001-draft), which is why this expiry is short.

DEV-EGRESS-LOOPBACK-001:C1.reason: GRANTED CONDITIONALLY AND NOT YET BUILT. [2026] VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-DEV-EGRESS-LOOPBACK-001 was decided 2026-07-31 and permits the dev-mode egress diversion only if ALL FIVE conditions hold; none is implemented, so there is nothing for a test to bind to yet. This is a waiver over a court order and is held to the higher bar the file requires: the expiry is SHORT (six weeks, not the usual year) precisely because the order is mine and freshly filed, and a waiver granted over one's own ruling is the worst version of the thing these files exist to remove. The diversion MUST NOT SHIP before the conditions are bound - C3 (the approval names the true destination) and C4 (the record says `diverted`, never `sent`) are the ratio itself, because an approval obtained on a false description of its effect is not an approval. If this entry expires with the feature unbuilt, the correct action is to withdraw the order's binding status or return to court, not renew.
